items.title: Different modes of stimulation at the Neiguan acupoint (PC6) regulate different EEG microstates under VR immersion conditions
items.summary: Introduction Acupuncture at the Neiguan acupoint (PC6) alleviates postoperative and chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting. Nevertheless, the central regulatory effects of PC6 stimulation on virtual reality motion sickness (VRMS), a form of physiological vertigo triggered by visual-vestibular sensory conflict, and the corresponding alterations in electroencephalogram (EEG) microstate characteristics remain unclear. items.title: Engineering Bidirectional Neuromodulation: A Review of Neural Excitation and Inhibition Technologies
items.summary: ABSTRACT Neuromodulation provides a means to perturb neural activity for investigating nervous system function and treating neurological disorders. Advances in stimulation strategies, molecular tools, functional materials and neural interfaces have progressively expanded the precision and versatility of such interventions. items.summary: Introduction Neuromodulatory interventions can produce overlapping adaptive outcomes despite engaging substantially different biological pathways. Pathway-centered approaches identify how interventions initially engage the nervous system and characterize pathway-specific mechanisms. Convergence across interventions raises an additional question: how can different biological routes influence overlapping domains of adaptive function? items.title: Prefrontal cortical morphometric covariance and cognitive task performance in healthy young adults: an exploratory analysis of Human Connectome Project data
items.summary: The prefrontal cortex (PFC) is implicated in many cognitive tasks, including working memory, reward-based decision-making, executive control, and metacognition. This exploratory analysis investigated whether individual expression of PFC cortical thickness and surface area covariance components is associated with cognitive task performance. The sample comprised Human Connectome Project (HCP) MRI data from 743 healthy adults (age 22–36+). items.title: Overcoming subject variability in P300 decoding based on quantification by deep learning
items.summary: Binary P300 decoding is a cornerstone of P300-based brain-computer interfaces, enabling applications such as assistive communication, neurorehabilitation, and cognitive monitoring. However, substantial subject variability in EEG patterns poses a major challenge to the development of generalized P300 decoders. items.summary: Background Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is increasingly recognized as a disorder of distributed neural dynamics. Resting-state fMRI combined with signal-complexity measures may provide new insights into alterations in spontaneous brain activity. This study investigated whether weighted permutation entropy (WPE), an amplitude-sensitive measure of temporal complexity, could identify regional abnormalities in AD and characterize their temporal and network-level features. items.title: Potential Mechanisms of Chlorogenic Acid in Cognitive Impairment: A Comprehensive Review
items.summary: Cognitive impairment (CI) is a clinical syndrome primarily affecting cognitive functions such as learning, memory, perception, and problem-solving. Its causes are heterogeneous, including neurological, psychiatric, metabolic, vascular, toxicological, and age-related factors. Currently, no specific and effective pharmacological therapies are available for CI in clinical practice. items.title: The prevalence of misreporting and misinterpreting correlation coefficients in biomedical literature
items.summary: Correlation coefficient is widely used in biomedical and biological literature. Yet, its frequent misuse and misinterpretation undermine the credibility and reproducibility of the scientific findings. items.summary: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) shows marked interindividual variation that complicates efforts to identify coherent neuroanatomical signatures. items.title: Learning and the Learner : A Comprehensive Theoretical Treatise on the Foundations, Theories, and Contemporary Dimensions of Human Learning — culminating in the Integral Learner Framework
items.summary: This treatise undertakes a comprehensive and critically systematic reconstruction of what is known about human learning and the person who learns. items.title: ANOS1 variant and PROK2 upregulation in familial Kallmann syndrome: integrative genetic, transcriptomic, and phenotypic study
items.summary: Kallmann syndrome (KS) arises from impaired development of the olfactory–GnRH neuronal system, yet the molecular consequences of individual gene defects remain poorly defined. In particular, the link between primary genetic variants and downstream transcriptional changes affecting neurodevelopmental pathways remains poorly understood. In the present study, we analyzed a Polish family with X-linked KS. items.title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and machine learning for outcome prediction in acute ischemic stroke: a retrospective study of 353 patients
items.summary: Background Acute ischemic stroke (AIS) remains a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Early prediction for clinical outcomes is essential for guiding therapy. Multiparametric Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers detailed characterization of ischemic tissue and may predict prognosis in AIS patients. This study assesses the prognostic value of multiparametric MRI parameters in predicting functional outcome, recurrence risk and mortality in AIS patients. items.summary: BACKGROUND: As mortality rates decline, life expectancy increases, and populations age, non-fatal outcomes of diseases and injuries are becoming a larger component of the global burden of disease. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. Despite its conceptual simplicity and broad applicability, it is rarely integrated into the undergraduate physics curriculum. items.summary: Abstract Exposure to maltreatment in childhood is posited to profoundly disrupt brain development with adverse consequences for cognitive development and health across the lifespan. Here we use “brain charts” from the largest available neuroimaging database to quantify individual brain volumes relative to normative brain growth distributions in 299 children, aged 3 to 13 years, including 123 children with clinically verified maltreatment exposure. items.summary: Background Teprotumumab, a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF-1R), is an approved targeted therapy for thyroid eye disease (TED). items.summary: Abstract Advanced brain age relative to chronological age may predict cognitive decline in healthy aging, but prospective evidence remains limited.
